aa31.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which drug blocks potassium, sodium and calcium channels as well as alpha and beta receptors?
opts: Correct. Amiodarone blocks potassium channels, inactivated sodium channels, calcium channels and alpha and beta receptors.
Dofetilide is a potent pure potassium channel blocker; the drug that blocks all of these is amiodarone.
Sotalol combines beta-blocking activity with potassium channel block only; amiodarone blocks all four targets.
Propafenone is a class IC sodium channel blocker with beta-blocking activity; amiodarone blocks all four targets.

aa31.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which antiarrhythmic's level rises when amiodarone is added?
opts: Adenosine is outside amiodarone's interaction list; amiodarone raises flecainide, procainamide, digoxin, warfarin and phenytoin.
Esmolol is outside amiodarone's interaction list; amiodarone raises flecainide, procainamide, digoxin, warfarin and phenytoin.
Correct. Amiodarone increases flecainide and procainamide, as well as digoxin, warfarin and phenytoin.
Magnesium sulfate is outside amiodarone's interaction list; amiodarone raises flecainide, procainamide, digoxin, warfarin and phenytoin.

aa31.io: List commonly used protocols and patient monitoring for antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which restriction applies to prescribing dofetilide?
opts: Correct. Dofetilide has limited availability, restricted to those with special training.
Intravenous-only use describes lidocaine, because of extensive first-pass metabolism; dofetilide needs special training.
Loading doses are for amiodarone, with its 40-day half-life; dofetilide's restriction is special prescriber training.
It is avoided with beta blockers
Avoiding beta blockers and calcium channel blockers is a digoxin caution; dofetilide's restriction is special prescriber training.

aa31.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which antiarrhythmic class prolongs repolarization by blocking potassium channels?
opts: Class I drugs block sodium channels and act on phase 0; the potassium channel blockers that prolong repolarization are class III.
Class II drugs are the beta receptor antagonists, which flatten phase 4; potassium channel blockers are class III.
Correct. Class 3 drugs are the potassium channel blockers that prolong repolarization: amiodarone, dofetilide and sotalol.
Class IV drugs block L-type calcium channels in the nodes; the potassium channel blockers are class III.

aa31.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Why may amiodarone require loading doses?
opts: A very short half-life (about 10 seconds) describes adenosine; amiodarone's half-life is very long.
Extensive first-pass metabolism is why lidocaine is given intravenously; amiodarone needs loading because of its long half-life.
It is eliminated unchanged by the kidneys
Elimination unchanged by the kidneys is dofetilide's; amiodarone needs loading because of its long half-life.
Correct. Amiodarone's half-life averages about 40 days, with slow onset and slow elimination, so loading doses may be needed.

aa31.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which amiodarone toxicity is listed as potentially fatal?
opts: Corneal deposits are an amiodarone eye toxicity, but the one listed as potentially fatal is pulmonary fibrosis.
Photosensitivity is an amiodarone skin effect, but the toxicity listed as potentially fatal is pulmonary fibrosis.
Blue-gray skin color is a visible amiodarone effect, but the toxicity listed as potentially fatal is pulmonary fibrosis.
Correct. Pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis are amiodarone's potentially fatal toxicity.

aa31.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which neurologic effects are listed for amiodarone?
opts: Seizures and nystagmus are part of lidocaine's central nervous system toxicity; amiodarone causes neuropathy and ataxia.
Correct. Amiodarone's neurotoxicity includes neuropathy, muscle weakness and ataxia.
Tinnitus, dizziness and blurred vision are quinidine's cinchonism; amiodarone causes neuropathy and ataxia.
Sedation and fatigue are listed for metoprolol and acebutolol; amiodarone causes neuropathy and ataxia.

aa31.io: Identify antiarrhythmic drug classes and commonly prescribed antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Sotalol combines the actions of which two antiarrhythmic classes?
opts: Sodium channel block with beta-blocking activity is propafenone, a class IC drug; sotalol is classes II and III.
Correct. Sotalol has beta-blocking (class II) activity and inhibits potassium channels (class III).
Blocking sodium and potassium channels describes flecainide, a class IC drug; sotalol is classes II and III.
Classes II and IV are separate drug groups (beta blockers and calcium channel blockers) that act on the nodes; sotalol is classes II and III.

aa31.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which change in the cardiac action potential is the signature of class III drugs?
opts: A slower, lower phase 0 upstroke is the class IA and IC picture; class III leaves the upstroke and delays phase 3.
Correct. Class III drugs prolong phase 3, so the action potential and the refractory period both last longer.
Earlier repolarization (a shortened phase 3) is the class IB picture; class III delays phase 3.
A flatter phase 4 in pacemaker cells is the class II and class IV picture; class III delays phase 3.

aa31.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Why can amiodarone cause hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism?
opts: It is a thyroid hormone analog
Correct. Amiodarone is an analog of thyroid hormone, and both hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism are on its toxicity list.
It blocks alpha and beta receptors
Amiodarone does block alpha and beta receptors, but its thyroid effects come from being an analog of thyroid hormone.
It is cleared unchanged by the kidneys
Elimination unchanged by the kidneys describes dofetilide; amiodarone's thyroid effects come from its thyroid hormone structure.
Sodium-potassium ATPase inhibition is digoxin's mechanism; amiodarone affects the thyroid because it is a thyroid hormone analog.

aa31.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Which pair of toxicities is listed for sotalol?
opts: Lupus-like syndrome and bone marrow suppression are procainamide's; sotalol causes torsades and bronchospasm.
Cinchonism and thrombocytopenia are quinidine's; sotalol causes torsades and bronchospasm.
Hypotension and edema are listed for verapamil and diltiazem; sotalol causes torsades and bronchospasm.
Correct. Sotalol's toxicities are torsades de pointes (from potassium channel block) and bronchospasm (from beta blockade).

aa31.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa31.q: Dofetilide is listed for which use?
opts: Slowing the ventricular rate in atrial flutter or fibrillation is digoxin's listed use; dofetilide is for normal rhythm.
Torsades de pointes is treated with intravenous magnesium sulfate, and dofetilide can cause it.
Correct. Dofetilide's listed indication is normal rhythm in atrial fibrillation.
Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia is listed for adenosine; dofetilide is for normal rhythm in atrial fibrillation.

aa32.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Which antiarrhythmic can turn the skin blue-gray?
opts: Dofetilide's listed adverse effects are torsades de pointes and marked QT prolongation; blue-gray skin is amiodarone's.
Sotalol's listed toxicities are torsades de pointes and bronchospasm; blue-gray skin is amiodarone's.
Correct. Blue-gray skin color, with photosensitivity, is on amiodarone's toxicity list.
Quinidine's listed toxicities include cinchonism and thrombocytopenia; blue-gray skin is amiodarone's.

aa32.io: Discuss potential drug-drug, drug-food, and drug-herb interactions with antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Amiodarone raises the levels of which pair of drugs?
opts: Codeine and morphine are the opioids named for quinidine's cytochrome P450 2D6 inhibition; amiodarone raises digoxin and warfarin.
Verapamil and diltiazem are calcium channel blockers to avoid alongside digoxin; amiodarone raises digoxin and warfarin.
Lidocaine and esmolol are intravenous agents outside amiodarone's list, which is digoxin, warfarin, flecainide, phenytoin and procainamide.
Correct. Amiodarone increases digoxin, warfarin, flecainide, phenytoin and procainamide.

aa32.io: Outline appropriate patient education for antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: A patient starting long-term amiodarone should be told to protect the skin from sunlight because of which effect?
opts: Correct. Photosensitivity is on amiodarone's toxicity list, along with a blue-gray skin color.
Flushing is listed for adenosine and magnesium sulfate, and sunlight does not trigger it; amiodarone causes photosensitivity.
Hypersensitivity is listed for lidocaine; the sun-related amiodarone effect is photosensitivity.
A lupus-like syndrome is procainamide's, more often in slow acetylators; amiodarone's sun-related effect is photosensitivity.

aa32.io: Describe absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of antiarrhythmic drugs
opts: Correct. Dofetilide is mainly eliminated unchanged in the kidneys.
Hepatic metabolism describes verapamil and diltiazem, hence caution in liver damage; dofetilide leaves unchanged by the kidneys.
Extensive first-pass metabolism describes lidocaine, which is why it is given intravenously; dofetilide leaves by the kidneys.
Acetylation describes procainamide, whose fast acetylators make more of its active metabolite; dofetilide leaves by the kidneys.

aa32.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Which is a listed indication for sotalol?
opts: Torsades de pointes is on sotalol's toxicity list; it is treated with magnesium sulfate.
Correct. Sotalol is listed for atrial flutter and fibrillation and for ventricular tachyarrhythmia.
Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome is listed for lidocaine and adenosine; sotalol is for atrial flutter and fibrillation.
Sick sinus syndrome is on the avoid list for verapamil and diltiazem; sotalol is for atrial flutter and fibrillation.

aa32.io: Identify indications for commonly used antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Which ventricular arrhythmia is a listed indication for amiodarone?
opts: Correct. Amiodarone is listed for recurrent ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation resistant to other drugs.
Ventricular ectopic beats are listed for propranolol; amiodarone is for ventricular tachycardia resistant to other drugs.
Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome is listed for lidocaine and adenosine, and it is not a ventricular arrhythmia; amiodarone is for refractory ventricular tachycardia.
Torsades de pointes is treated with magnesium sulfate, and prolonging repolarization can provoke it; amiodarone is for refractory ventricular tachycardia.

aa32.q: A patient with asthma needs a drug for atrial fibrillation. Which listed drug carries a bronchospasm risk?
opts: Dofetilide is a pure potassium channel blocker whose danger is torsades de pointes, not bronchospasm.
Amiodarone's lung toxicity is pneumonitis and pulmonary fibrosis over time; bronchospasm is listed for sotalol.
Correct. Sotalol has beta-blocking activity, and bronchospasm is on its toxicity list.
Digoxin's listed toxicities are gastrointestinal and central nervous system effects; bronchospasm is listed for sotalol.

aa32.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Class III antiarrhythmics prolong repolarization through which ion effect?
opts: More potassium leaving the cell would speed repolarization; class III drugs reduce potassium efflux to prolong it.
Correct. Class III drugs reduce potassium efflux, which prolongs phase 3 repolarization and the refractory period.
Reducing sodium influx in phase 0 is the class I mechanism; class III drugs reduce potassium efflux.
Blocking calcium influx through the L-type channel is the class IV mechanism; class III drugs reduce potassium efflux.

aa32.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Besides the lungs, thyroid, skin and eyes, which organ's dysfunction is listed for amiodarone?
opts: The kidneys are where dofetilide is mainly eliminated unchanged; amiodarone's listed organ dysfunction is hepatic.
Pancreatic injury is not on amiodarone's list; its organ toxicities are lung, thyroid, skin, eye, nerve and liver.
Correct. Hepatic dysfunction is on amiodarone's toxicity list.
Bone marrow suppression is listed for procainamide; amiodarone's listed organ dysfunction is hepatic.

aa32.io: Describe adverse effects of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Which adverse effect is the main danger of dofetilide?
opts: Pulmonary fibrosis is amiodarone's potentially fatal toxicity; dofetilide's danger is torsades de pointes.
Agranulocytosis is listed for propafenone; dofetilide's danger is torsades de pointes.
A lupus-like syndrome is procainamide's, more often in slow acetylators; dofetilide's danger is torsades de pointes.
Correct. Dofetilide's listed adverse effects are torsades de pointes and marked QT prolongation.

aa32.io: Describe the molecular mechanism of action of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Which antiarrhythmic is a potent pure potassium channel blocker?
opts: Amiodarone blocks potassium, sodium and calcium channels and alpha and beta receptors, so it is not a pure blocker.
Sotalol adds beta-blocking activity to its potassium channel block; the pure potassium channel blocker is dofetilide.
Flecainide blocks sodium and potassium channels in the ventricles and is class IC; the pure potassium channel blocker is dofetilide.
Correct. Dofetilide is a potent pure potassium channel blocker, used for normal rhythm in atrial fibrillation.

aa32.io: Summarize side effects and toxic manifestations of antiarrhythmic drugs
aa32.q: Which eye finding is listed among amiodarone's toxicities?
opts: Nystagmus is the early sign of lidocaine toxicity; amiodarone's listed eye finding is corneal deposits.
Correct. Corneal deposits are on amiodarone's toxicity list.
Glaucoma is a contraindication to disopyramide because of its anticholinergic action; amiodarone causes corneal deposits.
Blurred vision with tinnitus and dizziness is cinchonism from quinidine; amiodarone's listed eye finding is corneal deposits.
